s1.syndrome_frame: Progressively enlarging subcutaneous nodule with history of hepatocellular carcinoma
salient_findings: 8×4 cm subcutaneous mass over the right hypochondriac and flank regions
Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules on chest CT
Multiple nodules in liver segments 5 and 7 on abdominal CT
key_facts: Treated with partial hepatectomy, entecavir, transarterial chemoembolization, sorafenib, regorafenib, and pembrolizumab
Progressively enlarging right-flank subcutaneous nodule over two years
Vital signs: temperature 37.2°C, pulse 112/min, respiratory rate 19/min, blood pressure 114/78 mmHg

shortlist.label: hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: history of HBV-positive hepatocellular carcinoma and elevated alpha-fetoprotein

shortlist.label: extrahepatic hepatocellular carcinoma metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: progressively enlarging subcutaneous nodule and history of hepatocellular carcinoma

shortlist.label: primary soft tissue sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: subcutaneous mass invading the 12th rib and possibility of primary soft tissue sarcoma

shortlist.label: undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: aggressive nature of the subcutaneous mass and possibility of high-grade sarcoma

shortlist.label: liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: subcutaneous location of the mass and possibility of liposarcoma

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of HBV-positive hepatocellular carcinoma and the presence of a progressively enlarging right-flank subcutaneous nodule, along with multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules and liver nodules, suggests metastatic disease. The elevated alpha-fetoprotein level also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: This is the primary diagnosis, but it does not explain the subcutaneous nodule and other metastatic sites.

rejected.label: primary soft tissue sarcoma
rejected.why: Although possible, the patient's history of HCC and the presence of other metastatic sites make this less likely.

rejected.label: undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence to support this diagnosis, and the patient's history of HCC makes it less likely.

rejected.label: liposarcoma
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence to support this diagnosis, and the patient's history of HCC makes it less likely.
